Blog index; represents contributor/opinion listing templates.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-color-scheme: dark captures are pixel-identical (both 68,485 bytes), and the live CSS probe found zero color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border, and media colours.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, two 1,200 ms ifq-on-air animations remained running and the CSS probe found no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that stops non-essential pulse and auto-advance motion.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent interstitial obscures every audited content template on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots of the homepage, article, section and blog all show the privacy wall covering the primary content before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the full-screen first-load wall with a compact consent surface that leaves core headlines readable and offers immediate equal Accept and Reject actions.

findings.summary: The consent modal is not exposed as a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: While the visual overlay was present, the DOM probe found no dialog, role=dialog, role=alertdialog, or popover element.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement consent as a native dialog with an accessible name, focus trapping/restoration, Escape handling, and inert background content.

findings.summary: Navigation and consent chrome dominate the initial viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, two header rows plus the full-height consent panel leave the lead story only partly visible beneath the overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse duplicated mobile header rows and reserve the first viewport for the lead story once consent is handled.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt despite a navigation-heavy multi-page experience.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero view-transition declarations across the loaded styles, while recon identified many section and article routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable cross-document View Transitions for same-origin section/article links and disable them under reduced motion.

findings.summary: The multi-row sticky chrome does not use scroll-state-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no container scroll-state or scroll-timeline rules; mobile captures show two persistent header rows consuming vertical space.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state-aware CSS to shrink or hide secondary header chrome after scrolling while retaining orientation.

findings.summary: Repeated cards rely on page-level layout rather than component-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The rendered homepage contains many reused story cards, but the accessible stylesheet probe found zero @container rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reused story-card wrappers container-type and adapt typography/media with @container rules.

findings.summary: Several controls are too small or lack a visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 10 target-size failures on the homepage and 2 on the article; the focus probe found MENU, ABBONATI and ACCEDI with outline: none while :focus-visible matched.
findings.suggestedFix: Make targets at least 44 CSS px where practical and add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring to every control.

findings.summary: The article misses the good LCP threshold and both pages become interactive late.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured article LCP 3.1 s and TTI 14.3 s; homepage TTI was 22.1 s. The separate desktop trace measured LCP 1.79 s and TBT 19.5 ms, so the problem is condition-sensitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the article LCP element, delay non-critical tags, and break/defer post-load work until mobile LCP is below 2.5 s.

findings.summary: The mobile homepage shifts substantially during load.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout observer recorded CLS 0.223, including a 0.214 shift at about 1.54 s; the image audit found 45 of 100 images without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio to every image and reserve late banner/ad slots before they load.

findings.summary: Render-blocking CSS and heavy fonts delay content delivery.
findings.evidence: The HAR confirmed two VeryHigh-priority parser-inserted stylesheets; Lighthouse estimated 300 ms render-blocking savings, and two EB Garamond fonts transferred 296 KB and 282 KB. The main script was confirmed type=module and is not treated as blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, subset/preload the required font, and retain type=module for main.js.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 342 KiB unused JavaScript on the homepage and 543 KiB on the article, plus 24 KiB and 16 KiB unused CSS respectively.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused bundles and load analytics, advertising, comments, and media code only when their feature is used.

findings.summary: Accessible names and alternatives are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an untitled iframe and six label/name mismatches on the homepage; the article had two images without alt and one unnamed link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add missing alt text, iframe titles and link names, and align visible labels with accessible names.

findings.summary: Text colour contrast fails on both key templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported seven failing contrast nodes on both the homepage and article. Forced-colours remained readable, but normal-theme WCAG contrast still fails.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust failing foreground/background token pairs to WCAG AA and verify normal, dark and forced-colour modes.

findings.summary: Heading and keyboard structure is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage has an empty H1 followed by H3 topics, the article failed heading-order, and several focused top controls suppress their outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the homepage a meaningful H1, restore sequential headings, and add visible focus indicators to header controls.

findings.summary: Touch target spacing does not hold at mobile size.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 10 target-size failures on the homepage and 2 on the article. Reflow itself passed with 0 px overflow on three templates and only 1 px on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase small target boxes/spacing without breaking the already-successful narrow reflow.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a browser error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s errors-in-console audit found one browser error on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the captured runtime error and add console-error monitoring to representative template tests.

findings.summary: Many images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 45 of 100 homepage images without width/height; Lighthouse independently found 29 unsized images on home and 11 on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct intrinsic dimensions and aspect ratios to all editorial and chrome images.

findings.summary: Chrome reports inspector issues and avoidable legacy delivery.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse logged two DevTools Issues on home and one on article, plus about 17 KiB of legacy JavaScript on each.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools Issues and stop sending avoidable legacy JavaScript to modern browsers.

findings.summary: The document lacks baseline security headers and sets insecure cookies.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Two first-party cookies lacked Secure, including a 400-day SameSite=None cookie.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP, HSTS and nosniff, and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with the narrowest SameSite policy.

findings.summary: A large tracking footprint loads before a consent choice.
findings.evidence: The no-interaction load contacted 18 third-party origins and known Google Tag Manager, Ads and Analytics trackers. HAR recorded 70 of 72 requests and 2.06 MB of 2.15 MB as cross-origin, including three Google scripts totalling about 520 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Hold analytics and ad tags until a valid consent signal, remove redundant vendors, and batch necessary telemetry.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: No HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors policy was present on the main response.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options plus strict Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Consent presentation visually favours acceptance.
findings.evidence: On desktop, Accept is the only filled red button while Reject and Manage are outlined; on mobile Accept is placed first. Reject remains available, so this is a salience nudge rather than forced consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Give Accept and Reject equal visual weight and ordering; keep Manage preferences secondary but clearly available.

findings.summary: Image delivery leaves avoidable bytes and loading work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 255 KiB image savings on home and 164 KiB on article; the image audit found 43 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and 16 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive modern image sources, intrinsic dimensions and loading=lazy for below-fold editorial media.

findings.summary: Analytics and advertising work runs during the blocked first view.
findings.evidence: Before any consent interaction, the HAR loaded 23 scripts (894 KB) and 6 XHR/fetch requests; known analytics and advertising endpoints were already active.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate and defer analytics/ad work until consent and idle time; cancel background requests that no longer provide user value.

findings.summary: Third-party code and fonts are disproportionate for a text-news first view.
findings.evidence: The initial HAR transferred 2.15 MB, including 639 KB fonts and 894 KB scripts; Lighthouse’s fuller run reported 5,284 KiB total payload.
findings.suggestedFix: Set budgets for script, font and third-party bytes; subset fonts and remove vendors that do not justify their cost.

taskList.title: Rebuild consent as an accessible, non-blocking and visually neutral choice before loading tracking tags
Add CSP, HSTS, frame protection, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; secure all cookies
Reserve image space and optimise responsive/lazy image delivery to remove CLS and wasted bytes
Fix contrast, accessible names, heading order, iframe title, focus indicators and target sizing
Reduce unused and third-party JavaScript, subset/defer fonts, and shorten critical CSS/resource chains
Add preference-driven dark mode and reduced-motion overrides
Resolve console and DevTools Issues, then remove legacy delivery paths
Reduce persistent mobile chrome and make the header respond to scroll state
Adopt container queries for reused cards and validate them in narrow/wide placements
Use cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion-safe fallback for section/article navigation
